Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn and Child Health: Priorities for action!

content.text: Pakistan faces huge health challenges due to the existing burden of poor reproductive, maternal and child health and malnutrition as well as the emergence of non-communicable diseases.

To discuss these challenges, Aga Khan University's Centre of Excellence in Women and Child Health held a series of workshops and seminars on the AKU Stadium Road Campus in Karachi on February 19-22, 2015.
Pre-seminar workshops were organized on topics like women's empowerment for reproductive health, emergency obstetrical care, and emergency newborn care, amongst others.

The last in the series of events on Regional Mother Newborn and Child Health provided a unique platform to the faculty, students, nurses and researchers to come and present their studies via talks and poster presentations.

The series attracted a great deal of interest (with over 160 abstracts received and recorded in the Abstract Book) and was well attended by people from AKU as well as outside (approximately 250 people), including leaders of Pakistan Paediatric Association, Society of Obsterics and Gynaecology - Pakistan, Pakistan Medical Association, Federal Director General Health Services, Provincial Health Managers of MNCH, LHW and EPI programmes, health practitioners (doctors, nurses and paramedics staff), staff and students of AKU.
